# DragDrop unit fixtures must survive preceding browser-global teardown

## Context

The v13.2 candidate at `f1fbfe5c08196d418bd5ef5c80a99eff13a3cb30` has a red [Engine Tests unit job](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38107424093/job/114375788229): the refused-native-move case at `test/playwright/unit/main/addon/DragDrop.spec.mjs:105` throws `ReferenceError: window is not defined` at `src/main/addon/DragDrop.mjs:441`. Its retry passes; fail-on-flaky correctly leaves the job red.

## The Problem

The spec installs EventTarget-backed `window` and `document` once during module evaluation. The physical-window describe's beforeEach restores method stubs, but does not reinstall those globals. A controlled preceding-fixture deletion reproduces the exact current test body's exception; restoring its existing windowRef makes that same body pass, including its unhandled-rejection observer controls. This proves a fixture-lifetime vulnerability, not the identity of the original CI poisoner.

## The Architectural Reality

The main-thread drag path legitimately consumes browser window coordinates. Node unit tests own their simulated browser globals. The merged DomEvents/Touch fixture repair in #19218 establishes the neighboring per-test ownership pattern; it did not cover DragDrop.

Design authority: the hosted unit failure and the spec's existing EventTarget fixture contract. No production behavior is being changed.
Decision Record impact: none.
Contract Ledger: N/A; no consumed runtime surface changes.

## The Fix

Reinstall the spec's existing browser fixtures at the appropriate per-test boundary, preserve teardown restoration, and add a deterministic preceding-delete control that fails without the repair. Keep the refused-move observer's positive and negative assertions intact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Physical-window drag tests establish their own window/document fixtures before execution and restore borrowed global state correctly.
- [x] A preceding-delete regression fails without the repair and passes with it.
- [x] Existing refused-move and no-document-reset assertions remain effective; the focused spec and relevant neighboring fixtures pass.
- [x] The change is test-only, with no production guard, timeout increase, skip, retry-policy change or weakened assertion.

## Out of Scope

Identifying an unproven CI poisoner, changing native drag behavior, broad fixture infrastructure, and release publication.

## Avoided Traps

A green retry does not repair fixture ownership. Guarding production window reads would conceal a Node harness defect on a browser-only path.
